Vendor profile

Autodesk

Autodesk

By Gstarcademy Editorial Team Last reviewed 2026-06-23 Editorial process

Company Overview

Autodesk, Inc. is an American multinational software company headquartered in San Francisco, California. Founded in 1982 by John Walker and the co-creators of AutoCAD, Autodesk has grown from a single CAD product into the world's largest AEC/MFG design-software company with products spanning architecture, engineering, construction, media, and entertainment.

Autodesk's portfolio includes AutoCAD (2D/3D drafting), Revit (BIM), Inventor and Fusion 360 (MCAD), Civil 3D (civil engineering), 3ds Max and Maya (visualization and animation), and Navisworks (coordination). The company transitioned to subscription licensing in 2016, delivering products through the Autodesk Platform Services (formerly Forge) cloud ecosystem.

Market Segments

  • AEC (Architecture, Engineering, Construction): Revit, AutoCAD, Civil 3D, Navisworks, InfraWorks — dominant market share in BIM authoring and coordination.
  • Manufacturing: Inventor, Fusion 360, VRED, PowerMill — covering product design, simulation, CAM, and visualization.
  • Media & Entertainment: 3ds Max, Maya, Arnold — industry standards in VFX, game development, and architectural visualization.

Products in our knowledge base (7)

3ds Max

Autodesk's premium 3D modeling, animation, and rendering software, widely used for architectural visualization.

AutoCAD

The original commercial CAD platform — still the lingua franca of DWG-based 2D documentation across AEC, mechanical, and infrastructure work.

Civil 3D

Autodesk's civil-infrastructure design platform — alignments, profiles, corridors, surfaces, parcels, pipe networks, and pressure networks built on a DWG core.

Fusion 360

Autodesk's cloud-native unified design-and-make platform — parametric/direct hybrid modelling, CAM, sheet metal, simulation, electronics, and generative design in one subscription.

Inventor

Autodesk's Windows-native parametric MCAD — strong on large mechanical assemblies, sheet metal, frame generator, and integration with Autodesk Vault and Revit.

Navisworks

Autodesk's premium project review software enabling design coordination, clash detection, and 4D construction simulation.

Revit

Autodesk's flagship BIM authoring tool — the building model becomes the single source of truth for plans, sections, schedules, and clash detection.

Market Position & Strategy

Autodesk holds the dominant market position in AEC design software globally, with Revit and AutoCAD commanding the largest share of the BIM authoring and 2D drafting markets respectively. The company's 2016 transition from perpetual licenses to subscription-only pricing was disruptive but ultimately increased recurring revenue predictability and accelerated its shift to cloud-connected products.

The Autodesk Platform Services (APS, formerly Forge) strategy positions the company as an infrastructure provider rather than just a tool vendor. APS offers web APIs for file translation, model viewing, design automation, and data management, enabling third-party developers and enterprise customers to build custom workflows on top of Autodesk's data formats. This platform approach creates significant switching costs—once an organization's custom tools depend on APS APIs, migrating to a competing platform requires rebuilding those integrations.

In manufacturing, Autodesk's Fusion 360 represents a deliberate strategy to capture the small-to-midsize market that SolidWorks and Inventor traditionally served, but with a cloud-native, lower-price-point offering. The inclusion of CAM, simulation, electronics design, and generative design in a single subscription at a lower price point than traditional MCAD tools positions Fusion 360 as a disruptive force, though large enterprises still predominantly use Inventor, SolidWorks, or CATIA for production work.

Technology Platform

Autodesk's technology stack spans four decades of evolution. AutoCAD's DWG format remains the most widely used CAD file standard globally, though it is a proprietary binary format that Autodesk controls. Competing DWG implementations (Open Design Alliance's Teigha/ODA SDK) enable alternative products like BricsCAD and GstarCAD to read and write DWG files, but format compatibility remains an ongoing challenge as Autodesk updates the format with each AutoCAD release.

Revit uses a single-file database model (RVT) rather than the file-based approach of AutoCAD. This architectural choice—where the entire building model resides in one file with internal versioning for worksharing—provides data consistency but creates file-size scalability challenges on large projects. The Revit API (available in .NET) is extensively used by firms to automate repetitive tasks, though its single-threaded architecture limits computational performance for large-scale operations.

Fusion 360's cloud-native architecture stores project data in Autodesk's cloud (A360), with a local cache for offline editing. The modeling kernel combines Autodesk's own T-Spline technology (acquired from T-Splines Inc. in 2011) with a parametric/direct hybrid modeling engine. This architecture allows Autodesk to deploy updates continuously without requiring users to manage software versions, though it also means feature changes or pricing changes take effect unilaterally.

Learning Resources

Autodesk maintains one of the largest vendor-provided learning ecosystems in the CAD industry. Key resources include:

  • Autodesk Certification Program: Professional certifications for AutoCAD, Revit, Inventor, Civil 3D, and other products. Certifications are recognized across the AEC and manufacturing industries as baseline competency verification.
  • Autodesk Knowledge Network: Official documentation, tutorials, and community forums. The knowledge base covers product help, troubleshooting, and system requirements for all Autodesk products.
  • Autodesk University (AU): Annual conference (in-person and virtual) with hundreds of technical sessions. Recordings of AU sessions are freely available online and represent a substantial library of advanced-topic content from practitioners and Autodesk product teams.
  • Education licenses: Autodesk provides free educational licenses for students and educators, making its tools accessible for learning without financial barriers.
